items.title_en: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.title_zh: ThinkWorld：世界想象强化动力学链推理
items.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.
items.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在机器人操作上进展显著，但泛化受限于带动作标注的机器人演示数据的多样性与覆盖度。人类视频经验更广，却面临“数据可扩展”与“动作显式落地”之间的权衡。我们提出 ThinkWorld，将动作推理扎根于世界动力学，并用世界想象驱动的强化学习加以强化：把每个动作思考表示为动力学链（Chain-of-Dynamics, CoD），即一串离散运动 token，刻画从当前世界到未来状态的中间动力学，作为跨本体的通用动作表征。先用带标注演示初始化 CoD，再预测各 CoD 引发的未来，并强化预测更贴合观测结果者。由此，无动作标注的视频也能通过观测到的状态转移提供直接监督。仿真与真机实验验证了人到机器人的迁移，以及对未见任务与环境的泛化。
items.highlight_zh: 用动力学链统一动作表征，以世界想象做强化学习
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：VLA 模型在机器人操作上进步明显，但泛化受限于带动作标注的机器人演示数据的多样性与覆盖面；人类视频的行为与环境更丰富，却难以提供明确的动作监督，形成“要规模就没标签、要标签就没规模”的两难。
方法：提出 ThinkWorld 框架，把“动作思考”表示为动力学链（CoD）——一串离散运动 token，刻画从当前世界到未来状态的中间动力学，并作为跨本体通用的动作表征。先用带动作标注的演示初始化 CoD，再让模型预测每条 CoD 所导致的未来，凡是预测更贴合真实观测结果的 CoD 就被强化（强化学习）。
结果：这样，没有动作标注的视频也能通过观测到的状态转移提供直接监督，人类与机器人经验得以在同一推理空间中互相打磨。仿真和真机实验显示人→机器人迁移有效，并对未见任务与环境有较强泛化。
为何重要：它绕开了动作标注的瓶颈，为用海量人类视频训练机器人策略提供了一条可行路径。

rm.usage: 面向机械臂操作的 VLA 世界动力学链推理，与自瞄/导航/决策等赛项主线几乎无交集；最多只能作为工程机器人装配策略训练的远期思路参考，落地成本极高。

items.title_en: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation
items.title_zh: OSMA-Bench：家庭机器人导航中障碍物条件安全性的基准评测
items.abstract_en: Safe household navigation requires robots to regulate clearance and speed according to what an obstacle is and how close it is, without unnecessary conservatism. Yet existing evaluations do not test whether semantic safety distinctions are reflected in continuous motion. To that end, we introduce OSMA-Bench, an Obstacle-Conditioned Safe Motion Adaptation Benchmark built on spatially matched scenario sets that differ only in obstacle type. We also propose the \emph{Semantic Sensitivity Index} (SSI), which measures whether clearance and distance-dependent speed and smoothness follow the caution ordering of obstacles. Evaluating VLM-based and vision-language-action (VLA) policies on the benchmark, we find that neither consistently adapts its motion to obstacle safety, even with explicit safety prompts. Our analysis shows that the policies can correctly distinguish obstacles by safety relevance but fail to reflect this distinction in the motion parameters or actions they produce. For VLM-based policies, which recognize the obstacle and then generate a navigation program, adding an explicit parameter-inference step between these two stages improves adaptation. These findings expose a gap in \emph{semantic-to-motion grounding}, highlighting the need to translate semantic caution into appropriately safe motion.
items.abstract_zh: 安全的家庭导航要求机器人依据障碍物“是什么”和“有多近”来调节间距与速度，同时不过度保守。然而现有评测并未检验语义层面的安全区分是否体现在连续运动中。为此我们提出 OSMA-Bench：一个基于空间匹配场景集（各场景仅障碍物类型不同）的障碍物条件安全运动适配基准；并提出语义敏感度指数（SSI），衡量间距以及随距离变化的速度与平滑性能否遵循障碍物的谨慎度排序。评测基于 VLM 与 VLA 的策略后发现，即使给出显式安全提示，二者也未能稳定地依据障碍物安全性调整运动。分析表明，策略能正确区分障碍物的安全相关性，却无法把这种区分反映到输出的运动参数或动作上。对“先识别障碍、再生成导航程序”的 VLM 策略，在两步之间加入显式参数推断可改善适配。这些结果揭示了从语义到运动落实的缺口。
items.highlight_zh: OSMA-Bench 与 SSI 揭示语义安全未落到运动
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：家用机器人要安全导航，必须根据障碍物“是什么”和“离多近”来调节间距与速度，既不能冒进，也不该过度保守。但以往评测只看是否碰撞，没有检验语义层面的安全差异是否真的体现在连续运动参数里。
方法：作者构建 OSMA-Bench，其场景集在空间布局上严格匹配，只改变障碍物类型，从而剥离其他因素；并设计语义敏感度指数（SSI），考察间距、随距离变化的速度与平滑性是否遵循障碍物的“谨慎度排序”（例如比玻璃杯更靠近刀具应更小心）。
结果：评测基于 VLM 与 VLA 的策略后发现，即使显式给出安全提示，两类策略也不能稳定地按障碍物安全等级调整运动。进一步分析显示，它们其实能区分障碍物的安全相关性，却无法把这种理解转化为运动参数或动作。对“先识别障碍、再生成导航程序”的 VLM 策略，在两步中间插入显式的参数推断步骤可明显改善适配。
为何重要：它把问题定位在“语义→运动”的落实鸿沟，而非感知能力不足，为安全导航的模型与接口设计指明了改进方向。

rm.usage: 其"语义感知安全间距/速度"的评测思路（SSI 指标）可借鉴到哨兵导航：按障碍物类型（静止场地结构、己方/敌方机器人、可通行区域）分层评估避障时的减速与绕行是否符合谨慎度排序，用于调参与回归测试；但论文本身是家庭场景下 VLM/VLA 策略的评测研究，不能直接用于哨兵决策。

items.title_en: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
items.title_zh: 在几何中学习与推理：生成如何促进空间理解
items.abstract_en: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Second, we introduce 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing selected 2D cues, and find that generated depth provides larger reasoning gains on questions requiring fine-grained geometric discrimination. Building on this finding, we develop adaptive interleaved reasoning, in which GeoUG first drafts an answer and then decides whether to generate geometric evidence to confirm or revise it. We train this decision through reinforcement learning, balancing accuracy gains over retaining the draft against generation cost. GeoUG achieves circular accuracies of 97.9%, 90.8%, and 94.2% on CV-Bench-3D, 3DCueBench, and DA-2K with fewer generation calls than always generating.
items.abstract_zh: 图像与视频生成器能产出空间一致的视觉内容，但如何借此提升空间理解仍待探索。我们从训练时的几何监督与推理时的显式几何证据两个角度研究该问题，提出统一的几何理解与生成模型 GeoUG，将深度生成、多视图生成与空间理解整合。首先设计多尺度深度编解码器，使预训练视觉自编码器可用于度量深度生成，并表明联合训练对空间理解带来任务相关的增益。其次提出 3DCueBench，可在控制几何难度的同时平衡所选 2D 线索，发现生成的深度对需要细粒度几何判别的问题带来更大推理增益。据此提出自适应交错推理：GeoUG 先给出草稿答案，再决定是否生成几何证据以确认或修正，并用强化学习训练该决策，在准确率增益、保留草稿与生成开销之间取得平衡。在 CV-Bench-3D、3DCueBench 与 DA-2K 上循环准确率分别达 97.9%、90.8% 与 94.2%，且生成调用次数少于“始终生成”。
items.highlight_zh: 生成深度作几何证据，按需触发提升空间推理
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：图像与视频生成模型能产出空间一致的画面，但这种“会生成”的能力能否反过来帮助模型“看懂”三维空间（深度、多视图一致性），此前研究不足。
方法：作者提出统一的几何理解与生成模型 GeoUG，把深度生成、多视图生成与空间理解放进同一模型。要点有三：一是多尺度深度编解码器，让预训练的视觉自编码器也能生成带真实尺度的深度；二是提出 3DCueBench，可调节几何难度并平衡 2D 线索，用来查清“生成深度在什么问题上最有用”；三是自适应交错推理——GeoUG 先写草稿答案，再判断是否值得生成几何证据来确认或修正，并用强化学习训练这一决策，在答对率、保住草稿与生成开销之间权衡。
结果：联合训练对空间理解有任务相关的增益；生成深度在需要细粒度几何判别的问题上帮助最大。在 CV-Bench-3D、3DCueBench、DA-2K 上分别达到 97.9%、90.8%、94.2% 的循环准确率，且生成调用次数少于“每次都生成”。
为何重要：说明“会生成”能反哺“会理解”，并给出了何时值得调用生成的省算力策略。

rm.usage: 深度/多视图几何生成与空间理解，与装甲板点阵识别、能量机关打击等赛项需求的关联很弱；若硬套，只能作为单目深度估计辅助（如飞镖或雷达视觉测距）的间接参考。

items.title_en: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
items.title_zh: EgoThumb：视觉驱动的多余度机器拇指，实现自主抓取与持握辅助
items.abstract_en: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.
items.abstract_zh: 多余度机器手指通过让单手完成通常需要双手协同的“握持并操作”任务来增强人的灵巧性。但现有装置常受限于笨重硬件，只能与大物体交互，且依赖缺乏环境上下文的显式手部动作触发。为此我们提出 EgoThumb：一款完全开源、视觉驱动的多余度机器拇指。它采用紧凑的双肌腱驱动手指，将驱动单元移至前臂，减轻末端重量并实现精确的主动关节控制；系统使用视觉模仿学习策略，将掌心朝向相机的第一视角图像直接映射为连续关节位置，从同时捕捉手与目标物体的视觉线索中隐式解码人的意图，从而实现稳健的自主操作，并在不同用户与环境中表现出较强泛化。所有硬件设计与软件实现均已完全开源。
items.highlight_zh: 视觉驱动、驱动前移的开源多余度机器拇指
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：多余度机器手指（俗称“第六指”）能让单手完成原本需要两只手配合的“先握住、再操作”任务，比如一手稳住瓶子、另一“指”拧开瓶盖。但已有装置往往笨重、只能应付大物体，且需要人做出明确的手部动作来触发，机器并不理解当前环境与意图。
方法：作者提出 EgoThumb，一款完全开源的视觉驱动多余度机器拇指。硬件上采用紧凑的双肌腱驱动手指，把电机等驱动器挪到前臂，既减轻手部末端负担，又实现各关节的精确主动控制。软件上训练视觉模仿学习策略，把掌心朝向相机拍到的第一视角图像，直接映射成连续的关节位置指令；由于画面里同时包含手和目标物体，模型可以隐式读出人的抓取意图。
结果：系统能稳健地自主完成抓取与持握辅助，并在不同用户与使用环境下表现出较强泛化。硬件设计与软件代码全部开源。
为何重要：它把“猜意图”交给视觉、把重量负担移出手部，为可穿戴辅助操作设备提供了一个轻量、可复现、易推广的方案。
items.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

items.title_en: Learning Scene Coordinate Reconstruction from Unposed Images via Pose Graph Optimization
items.title_zh: 从无位姿图像中通过位姿图优化学习场景坐标重建
items.abstract_en: Learning-based structure-from-motion methods such as ACE-Zero have demonstrated strong performance in estimating cameraposes and scene coordinates from unordered image collections without requiring ground truth supervision. However, the lack of global and multi-view consistency constraints in ACE-Zero can lead to pose drift and misalignment, particularly in complex or ambiguous scenes. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates pose graph optimization (PGO) into ACE-Zero to refine camera poses and suppress incorrect refinements. We construct pose graphs directly from ACE-Zero outputs by extracting relative pose constraints from predicted scene coordinates. Furthermore, we introduce an uncertainty-aware optimization strategy by estimating confidence scores using geometric priors, including epipolar and optical flow consistencies across views. Our approach improves the robustness and accuracy of pose estimation, demonstrating that global geometric reasoning can effectively complement learning-based inference in structure-from-motion.
items.abstract_zh: ACE-Zero 等基于学习的三维重建方法无需真值监督，即可从无序图像集合中估计相机位姿与场景坐标，性能表现突出。但 ACE-Zero 缺乏全局与多视图一致性约束，在复杂或歧义场景中容易出现位姿漂移与错位。本文提出一种混合框架，把位姿图优化（PGO）嵌入 ACE-Zero，用来精化相机位姿并抑制错误的更新。该方法直接从 ACE-Zero 输出的预测场景坐标中提取相对位姿约束来构建位姿图，并引入不确定性感知优化策略，利用对极几何与跨视图光流一致性等几何先验估计置信度。实验表明，该方法提升了位姿估计的鲁棒性与精度，说明全局几何推理能有效补充基于学习的 SfM 推断。
items.highlight_zh: 用位姿图优化为 ACE-Zero 补上全局一致性约束
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】ACE-Zero 一类方法能在没有真值标注的情况下，从一堆无序照片里同时推断相机在哪、场景点在哪，效果不错。但它只看局部，缺少全局和多视图之间的一致性约束，因此在场景复杂或存在歧义时，估计出的相机轨迹会逐渐漂移、彼此错位。

【方法】作者提出一个混合框架：保留 ACE-Zero 的预测能力，在其输出之上再做全局优化。第一步，从 ACE-Zero 预测的场景坐标里反推出两两相机之间的相对位姿约束，据此构建位姿图；第二步，在优化时引入不确定性感知策略，用几何先验（跨视图的对极几何一致性、光流一致性）为每条约束打置信度分，让可靠的约束说话、可疑的约束被压住。

【结果】加入位姿图优化后，位姿估计的鲁棒性和精度都有提升，原本容易发生的漂移与错误精化被明显抑制。

【意义】这说明「学习式推断 + 全局几何推理」是一条可行的互补路线：神经网络负责从图像中提取信息，经典几何优化负责保证整体一致，从而让无需监督的 SfM 在更难的场景里也站得住脚。

rm.usage: 无位姿图像下的场景坐标回归+位姿图优化，可作为视觉重定位方案：赛前用场地多视角图像离线建场景坐标图，比赛中相机图像直接回归位姿，用于哨兵里程计漂移后的重定位或雷达场端相机标定；但 RM 场地纹理稀疏、结构对称，需大量改造与实测。

items.title_en: SAGE: Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts for Point Cloud Registration
items.title_zh: SAGE：面向点云配准的语义增强几何专家模型
items.abstract_en: Point cloud registration is an essential task for scene reconstruction, requiring the alignment of partially overlapping point clouds. Under low-overlap conditions, this task remains challenging because existing geometry-only methods cannot distinguish geometrically similar but semantically distinct structures (e.g., TV corners vs. desk corners and chair legs vs. table legs), resulting in incorrect correspondences. To address this geometric ambiguity, we present Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts (SAGE), which integrates frozen pre-trained point cloud semantic representations into the registration pipeline without requiring additional sensors or fine-tuning the semantic encoder. To effectively leverage these semantic distinctions, SAGE employs a Semantic-Guided Mixture of Experts (SG-MoE) architecture. Through semantic-aware routing, SG-MoE enables each expert to specialize in distinct semantic-geometric patterns, reducing mismatches that confound geometry-only methods. With a structure-aware estimator, SAGE achieves the highest registration recall on 3DLoMatch while remaining competitive on 3DMatch. When evaluated with the same number of refinement iterations, SAGE further achieves the highest inlier ratio and registration recall on both benchmarks. These results indicate that frozen semantic representations provide effective cues for resolving geometric ambiguity in low-overlap registration.
items.abstract_zh: 点云配准是场景重建的关键任务，需对齐部分重叠的点云。低重叠条件下该任务仍具挑战：仅依赖几何的方法无法区分几何相似但语义不同的结构（如电视角与桌角、椅腿与桌腿），导致错误对应。为此，作者提出语义增强几何专家（SAGE），将冻结的预训练点云语义表征引入配准流程，无需额外传感器，也无需微调语义编码器。SAGE 采用语义引导的专家混合（SG-MoE）架构，通过语义感知路由使各专家专注于不同的语义-几何模式，减少纯几何方法易犯的误匹配。配合结构感知估计器，SAGE 在 3DLoMatch 上取得最高配准召回率，在 3DMatch 上保持竞争力；在相同精化迭代次数下，两个基准上的内点率与召回率均最优。结果表明，冻结语义表征能为解决低重叠配准中的几何歧义提供有效线索。
items.highlight_zh: 冻结语义表征 + 语义路由专家混合破解低重叠配准歧义
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】把两次扫描得到的点云对齐（配准）是三维重建的基础。当两次扫描只有很小一部分重叠时，现有只依赖几何形状的方法容易出错：场景里常常有形状几乎一样但含义不同的东西，比如电视的方角和桌子的方角、椅腿和桌腿，几何上难以分辨，于是匹配到错误的位置。

【方法】作者提出 SAGE，把预训练好的点云语义模型「冻结」后直接接入配准流程，既不需要额外传感器，也不需要重新训练语义网络。为了让语义信息真正发挥作用，SAGE 设计了语义引导的专家混合架构（SG-MoE）：多个专家网络各管一类语义-几何模式，路由模块根据语义信息决定由哪些专家处理，从而把靠形状分不开的结构区分开。最后用结构感知的估计器输出位姿。

【结果】SAGE 在低重叠基准 3DLoMatch 上取得最高配准召回率，在 3DMatch 上保持竞争力；在同等精化迭代次数下，两个基准的内点率和召回率均为最优。

【意义】工作表明，现成的语义特征即使不微调，也能有效缓解低重叠配准中的几何歧义，为配准提供了一条成本低、易复用的改进思路。

rm.usage: 语义增强的低重叠点云配准，可用于雷达/场端多传感器点云对齐、多帧点云地图拼接以及在低重叠下把敌方机器人点云与地图/多目标轨迹关联，降低相似几何结构的误匹配；需按机器人目标尺度重训语义分支。
rm.task: 雷达目标探测与信息融合

items.title_en: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
items.title_zh: SVIn+：融合三维声纳、视觉惯性、水压与DVL的鲁棒水下状态估计多模态框架
items.abstract_en: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. In this paper, we tackle this problem, by presenting SVIn+, a multi-sensor framework for robust state estimation of AUVs equipped with an IMU, cameras, a water-pressure sensor, a Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), and a compact 3D sonar. This framework extends an established open-source state-of-the-art visual-inertial SLAM, SVIn, by integrating water-pressure and DVL measurements into a tightly-coupled nonlinear optimiza- tion formulation resulting in improved estimates. To leverage the structural information of recently available 3D acoustic sonars while maintaining computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical architecture that incorporates estimates from a decoupled front-end via KISS-ICP, treated as relative pose factors within the factor graph. The proposed framework is validated through field deployments in a shipwreck and coral reef, demonstrating drift mitigation and global consistency. To support further research in underwater multi-modal fusion, the code and the datasets can be found on project website https://cmburgul.github.io/projects/svin+/ https://dartmouthrobotics.github.io/svin-plus

items.title_en: UT-HMR: Uncertainty-Guided Temporal Modeling for Robust 3D Human Mesh Recovery
items.title_zh: UT-HMR：面向鲁棒三维人体网格恢复的不确定性引导时序建模
items.abstract_en: Monocular 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) remains unreliable under weak observations caused by long camera-to-person distances, occlusion, and motion blur. In challenging scenarios such as sports, these factors make the problem highly ambiguous, as different 3D poses may yield similar 2D projections. This ambiguity is especially severe for one-stage HMR, which recovers all meshes directly from the full image without person crops or external 2D cues. To handle this ambiguity, we present UT-HMR ( Uncertainty-guided Temporal HMR), to our knowledge the first one-stage HMR framework to capture correlated pose uncertainty across joints. Each person query predicts a Gaussian distribution over the full SMPL pose with a compact low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance, which is converted into joint-wise precision weights for heteroscedastic supervision while keeping inference deterministic. Temporal early fusion further injects neighboring-frame evidence before pose decoding, supplying the visual evidence needed to resolve the ambiguity that the uncertainty captures. With a lightweight ViT-B backbone, UT-HMR achieves state-of-the-art results on VIP-HockeyPose-v2 (ice hockey) and WorldPose (soccer), reducing MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, and PVE by up to 4.7%, 3.8%, and 5.6%, and remains competitive on 3DPW against methods with larger backbones and higher input resolutions.

items.title_en: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: 基于免模仿速度评分的闭环感知规划用于端到端自动驾驶
items.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. We realize this paradigm as Closed-Loop Aware Planning for Autonomous Driving (CLAP-AD), a plug-in planning head that integrates with existing end-to-end driving models and, to our knowledge, is the first to enable explicit test-time control over their speed selection without speed-conditioned training. On Bench2Drive-Speed, CLAP-AD sets a new state of the art Speed-Adherence Score of 82.53, topping TFv6, the strongest baseline on this metric, by 12.9 points while retaining strong closed-loop driving performance. On Bench2Drive, it improves driving score by +28.5 and +32.7 over UniAD and VAD, and on NAVSIM v2, built on real-world driving data, EPDMS by +6.1 over its backbone. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io
items.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 17 pages (8-page main paper, references, and supplementary material), 5 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io. \c{opyright} 2027 IEEE. items.title_en: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View
items.title_zh: 重审直接控制：通过鸟瞰图遥操作全尺寸自动驾驶车辆的传感器融合效能实地评估
items.abstract_en: In autonomous driving, robot teleoperation serves as a critical safety fallback mechanism, requiring operators to assume direct control in the event of system failure. While recent research has pivoted toward high-level supervisory control or simulation-based studies, these approaches often fail to capture the physical dynamics and sensory demands of driving a full-scale vehicle. To address this gap, we evaluated the impact of spatial data representation on operator performance using a real car-sized vehicle in a field experiment with $N = 18$ participants. We compared three visualization interfaces: (i) a standard camera feed baseline, with two bird's-eye views (BEV) from (ii) a raw LiDAR point cloud, and (iii) a sensor fusion of LiDAR and camera data streams. Contrary to prior passive observation studies suggesting that sensor-fusion BEV may hinder awareness, our active-control results demonstrate that such representation significantly outperforms the standard LiDAR BEV in perceived usability ($p \leq 0.0001$) and cognitive task load ($p = 0.01$, NASA-TLX score: 34.58/100) while also being significantly better than the Camera-only view ($p = 0.043$). The fused interface also led to statistically significant reductions in task completion time ($p = 0.0461$) and superior usability (SUS: 77.9/100) compared to those of the Camera-only and LiDAR-only views. By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, we demonstrate that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand. These findings challenge existing teleoperation conventions and provide an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.
items.comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

items.title_en: Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup for Robust Camera-Based 3D Object Detection
items.title_zh: 稀疏恢复鸟瞰图模型汤用于鲁棒的基于相机的三维目标检测
items.abstract_en: Camera-based bird's-eye view (BEV) perception methods such as Fast-BEV have demonstrated promising results with fast inference speed and competitive accuracy. However, their robustness to real-world corruptions remains insufficiently explored, posing risks for autonomous driving deployment where environmental variations are inevitable. In this paper, we propose Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup (SR-BEVS), a sparse recovery learning approach that simultaneously improves clean accuracy and corruption robustness without requiring additional data or architectural modifications. Our method identifies pruning candidates based on layer-wise weight magnitudes, applies random pruning to create diverse sparse models, and retrains each model with a randomly sampled learning rate. By averaging these diverse recovered models into a single dense model, we achieve enhanced robustness against various corruptions while introducing zero inference overhead. We further provide a mode connectivity analysis demonstrating that our pruning-based diversification preserves the connected low-loss basin necessary for stable weight averaging. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate up to 33.8% improvement in corruption robustness and a 1.8% gain in clean accuracy over the Fast-BEV baseline, with consistent improvements across sensor noise, weather distortions, and illumination changes. Our simple yet effective approach may be applicable to other BEV models.

items.title_en: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
items.title_zh: GameVerse：面向长时程交互式世界建模的分钟级游戏玩法数据集
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video dataset purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling. GameVerse contains 69.7K clips spanning 1,655 hours and 349.6 million frames across diverse first- and third-person gameplay, including 1,358 hours of continuous two-minute sequences, an order of magnitude longer than prior datasets. Clips pass through a unified pipeline of scene-consistent segmentation, quality filtering, camera pose estimation, and event-based caption annotation. Each clip is paired with a temporally stable camera trajectory that remains coherent across minutes, together with captions that separate static scene context from dynamic foreground events and align to event boundaries rather than fixed time windows. Comprehensive analysis shows that GameVerse surpasses existing public datasets in scale, diversity, and annotation quality. Experiments further demonstrate that training on GameVerse substantially extends the temporal horizon of interactive world models.

items.title_en: AdaDexTrack: Dynamic Modulation for Adaptive and Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation Tracking
items.title_zh: AdaDexTrack：面向自适应与可泛化灵巧操作跟踪的动态调制
items.abstract_en: Language is a natural way to command robots, but converting a single instruction into a long-horizon, contact-rich hand-object interaction remains challenging: synthesized references are noisy, human-to-robot retargeting introduces embodiment bias, and fixed-reference tracking lets small errors snowball. We address this with AdaDexTrack, a modulator-in-the-loop framework for language-conditioned manipulation tracking. A distilled generalist tracker serves as the skill carrier, while a tightly aligned modulator performs three feedback corrections: reference modulation (continual adjustment of what to track), object-latent modulation (online adaptation of the object representation to recruit suitable skills), and positional-target modulation (small state-dependent refinements for execution). The tracker is learned via large-scale specialist to generalist distillation on a corpus of language-conditioned hand-object trajectories; the modulator is trained with RL under the same task objective, ensuring tight coupling. Across large-scale evaluations, AdaDexTrack consistently outperforms prior SOTA on unseen-trajectory and unseen-object sets in both average tracking error and success rate, demonstrating robustness and generalization. We further show zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on real hardware, where adding the modulator yields substantial gains over a tracker-only variant. AdaDexTrack reframes language-conditioned dexterous manipulation as modulated tracking, replacing the open-loop, fixed-reference tracking with in-loop modulation that adjusts the reference, object latent, and positional target, yielding drift-resistant execution from noisy text references.
items.comment: CVPR 2026. 18 pages, 14 figures, including supplementary material. Project page: https://janebek.github.io/AdaDexTrack/

items.title_en: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning
items.title_zh: HIDRA：面向无回放终身模仿学习的分层双路由注意力
items.abstract_en: Robotic agents operating in real-world environments must adapt continuously from a stream of multimodal demonstrations, often under constraints that preclude storing or revisiting past data. In this replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning setting, sequential updates can progressively distort the representation space, making expert-based approaches particularly sensitive to routing interference, causing expert selection to degrade over time. We propose HIDRA, a structured routing framework that mitigates this issue through a hierarchical dual-attention mechanism, which decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement. To further stabilize routing under representation drift, HIDRA introduces a key-level geometric regularization that enforces both alignment within tasks and separation across tasks. The resulting approach enables reliable expert selection while supporting an expandable set of experts for continual adaptation. We evaluate HIDRA on several LIBERO benchmark suites, including more challenging variants with heterogeneous task sequences and paraphrased language instructions. Our approach consistently outperforms both replay-free and replay-based baselines, improving AUC and forward transfer while maintaining low forgetting, with stronger gains under high interference and language variation. The code is available at: https://github.com/yfqi/HIDRA.
items.comment: This is the authors' preprint, accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Conference. The final version is available in the NeurIPS 2026 proceedings

items.title_en: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
items.title_zh: 基于路由集成与轨迹归因的多目标强化学习
items.abstract_en: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency. Then, we design routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward. Finally, we consider trajectory selection as another approach to mitigate objective conflict, and design a kernel surrogate trajectory attribution algorithm that estimates how feedback signals from a set of trajectories influence policy learning on other trajectories. The kernel can capture nonlinear interactions such as synergy and antagonism between trajectories. We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.
items.comment: 30 pages. To appear at NeurIPS 2026 (extended version)

items.title_en: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
items.title_zh: 面向去中心化LLM协作的信念条件多智能体演员-评论家
items.abstract_en: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft game-playing, web searching and tool-using tasks show that BCMAAC improves task performance and collaborative behavior compared to naive actor-critic baselines. The improvements are particularly pronounced in multi-turn tasks with richer contextual information, where belief modeling provides a clear advantage.
items.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop PTA: From Pretrained Representations to Acting Agents. 18 pages, 3 figures

items.title_en: PosePlaner: Denoising Any Feed-Forward Pose Predictor from Pairwise Planar Geometry
items.title_zh: PosePlaner：利用成对平面几何对任意前馈位姿预测器进行去噪
items.abstract_en: Recent multi-view Transformers (e.g., DUSt3R and VGGT) have advanced 3D reconstruction by scaling training data and model capacity from two views to many views and long sequences, subsuming the classical SfM/SLAM pipeline of feature extraction, matching, and pose estimation in a single feed-forward pass. Yet this subsumption hides the interfaces between pipeline stages---correspondences, geometry, and pose are entangled in a single forward pass, leaving supervised fine-tuning as the major path to improvement and offering no mechanism to correct predictions from geometric evidence at test time. We propose PosePlaner to close this gap by reviving the classical coupling between correspondences and pose via flow matching, treating pose refinement as a conditional generation problem that takes coarse geometric matches and initial pose as input condition and fuses the resulting pose hypotheses into a single refined estimate, providing a continuous, data-driven analog of RANSAC voting. Our method is trained efficiently on two-view data, yet serves as a periodic refiner for streaming n-view pose estimators with no retraining. Empirically, it corrects failures of feed-forward predictors, substantially improves correspondence-based solvers, and reduces accumulated drift in long streaming sequences.

items.title_en: UniQuery: Unifying Vision Models with a Joint Query Head for Cross-Domain Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
items.title_zh: UniQuery：以联合查询头统一视觉模型用于跨域行人属性识别
items.abstract_en: Pedestrian Attribute Recognition (PAR) predicts semantic attributes of individuals, such as gender, age, clothing and accessories, and its descriptions support attribute-based person retrieval and person re-identification. However, accurately recognizing fine-grained attributes across domains remains challenging due to occlusion, appearance variations, and shifts in image distributions. Ensembles of independently trained foundation encoders combine their logits with fixed fusion weights, so every attribute uses the same mix and the encoders are never trained together. We propose UniQuery, which instead jointly fine-tunes DINOv3 and CLIP for attribute-specific fusion. It combines two query heads, one for each encoder, with a joint query head whose attribute queries attend to tokens from both encoders, and the prediction is the average of the logits of the three query heads. We evaluate UniQuery on the benchmark of the UPAR Challenge 2027 at the WACV 2027 Real-World Surveillance workshop, where models are trained on PA100k, PETA and Market-1501 with a shared set of attributes. In leave-one-dataset-out experiments, UniQuery outperforms the independent ensemble in Challenge_Avg on both held-out datasets. Ablations show that learning fusion over independently trained encoders does not improve upon logit averaging in the mean over the two held-out datasets, while freezing the encoders lowers the Challenge_Avg of UniQuery. On the hidden test set of the benchmark, UniQuery achieves a Challenge_Avg of 0.8001.
items.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to the 7th Real-World Surveillance Workshop (RWS) at WACV 2027

items.title_en: Models Verify Sufficiency, Not Validity: Usable Falsehoods Evade the Checks that Gaps Trigger
items.title_zh: 模型验证的是充分性而非有效性：可用的虚假陈述会规避由缺口触发的检查
items.abstract_en: Ask a model "how many settlements did the Normans control?" and it answers that the passage does not say. Tell it "given that the Normans controlled 12 settlements of 400 inhabitants, what is the total?" and it computes 4,800. Nothing was added to the passage; the unsupported fact merely became usable. Benchmarks for unanswerable questions are built almost entirely by omission, deleting the fact a question needs and scoring refusal, so they never probe this. Holding source support fixed and varying only whether an unsupported premise is usable, flagging drops 8-30 points and commitment to an answer rises 1.5-2.3x on GSM8K across four models spanning two families and 2B-26B; all 16 paired contrasts remain significant after Holm correction. Two further manipulations reproduce it, one also on SQuAD: a fact asserted rather than asked about, and a corrupted intermediate value rather than a removed one. Models articulate the exact gap they then ignore, stating that "there is no financial information provided" for an inert premise and silently adopting a fabricated price for the same item. We read these as one behaviour: whether a model checks depends substantially on whether usable material is present, even when source support is held fixed. Because the main design never instructs models to reject premises introduced in the question, adopting such a premise can also be read as conditional reasoning, and we delimit what the design does and does not show. In the judging seat the pattern differs: asked whether the answer follows, judges pass solutions with a required step deleted 78-99% of the time at every scale tested. A natural prompt-level mitigation lowers accuracy by 22 points without improving detection.
items.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Self-Evolving Diversity-Driven Search for Robust AI Systems (EvoRobust). 5 pages plus references, 3 tables

items.title_en: Bracketing Shows the Way: Adaptive Multi-Exposure Policy as Input for Robust Visual SLAM
items.title_zh: 包围曝光指明方向：自适应多曝光策略作为鲁棒视觉SLAM的输入
items.abstract_en: Rapid illumination transitions can disturb Visual SLAM (VSLAM) by saturating images before the Automatic Exposure (AE) policy adapts, removing the visual correspondences needed to maintain tracking. Our proposed methods mitigate this disturbance at two levels: B-Adapt acquires adaptive exposure brackets to cover the scene dynamic range while promoting photometric overlap, and BVSLAM directly uses the multi-exposure sequence as constraints in a factor graph state estimator without relying on High Dynamic Range (HDR) merging. We evaluate both methods against state-of-the-art approaches in nominal environments and during a repeated tunnel-exit transition at an emulated vehicle speed of 32 m s-1. In the tunnel, combining our B-Adapt with BVSLAM reduces the state estimation error by 78 % compared with AE images. These results suggest that bracketing efficiently improves visual pose estimation robustness to rapid illumination disturbances while retaining low error under nominal conditions. Our code is available at https://github.com/norlab-ulaval/bracketing-shows-the-way.
items.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2027)

items.title_en: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning
items.title_zh: CausGround：面向自适应具身规划的因果交互定位
items.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show promising reasoning capabilities, but reliable physical interaction requires planning that accounts for when actions are executable and how they change the world. These preconditions and effects are environment-dependent and often not captured by MLLMs, making adaptation challenging. Yet existing approaches either require costly environment-specific training or rely on unstructured interaction experience that is difficult to reuse. Therefore, we introduce CausGround, a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into reusable action-centered causal knowledge. CausGround identifies action preconditions and effects and organizes them in a factorized world-state representation capturing object attributes and inter-object relations. At planning time, task-relevant causal dependencies are grounded in current observations to support backward reasoning over preconditions and forward reasoning over effects for action selection and multi-step planning. We evaluate CausGround on simulated high-level planning, interaction reasoning, and real-world robot manipulation. On adapted VirtualHome and RoboCasa benchmarks, CausGround improves vision-based high-level planning across MLLM backbones, increasing average task success from 24.9% to 53.3% on VirtualHome and closed-loop planning success from 43.0% to 57.0% on RoboCasa. On SWITCH, average interaction reasoning accuracy increases from 25.8% to 31.9%, indicating improved action selection, recovery, and verification. Moreover, real-world experiments show that CausGround reasons backward from MLLM-interpreted goals to derive executable high-level action sequences for sequential manipulation. These results demonstrate that reusable action preconditions and effects support long-horizon embodied planning across diverse environments without parameter updates.

items.title_en: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
items.title_zh: 提升灵巧性与安全性：实现效果显著优异的在手物体位姿到达
items.abstract_en: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.

items.title_en: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: EnvSched：面向 rollout 高效智能体强化学习的环境感知调度
items.abstract_en: As executable environments for language agents scale, generating and verifying their rollouts becomes increasingly expensive. Under finite rollout budgets, this raises an important question: can data management at the environment level make agentic reinforcement learning (RL) more efficient by organizing, evaluating, and scheduling task instances together with the environments that determine their tools, states, transitions, and verification? To address this question, we introduce EnvSched (Environment-aware Scheduling), an online scheduler that learns from rollout history. EnvSched assigns scheduling value through two complementary modeling choices: exploitation prioritizes tasks likely to provide informative reward differences, while coverage spreads each batch across underobserved environments and interaction patterns. EnvSched organizes environment--task pairs as nodes in a dual-relation graph, with within-environment edges capturing task semantics and shared tool, state, and verifier structure, and cross-environment edges capturing abstract execution and reward topology. By propagating historical rollout statistics along both edge types, it predicts within-task reward variance. These predictions guide a scheduler that allocates each batch to tasks with high predicted reward variance and underobserved environments and tasks. Environment quotas and a similarity penalty further limit concentration and redundancy, yielding informative and diverse batches without additional pilot rollouts. In RL on Qwen3-8B, EnvSched achieves an average score of 48.81 across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent after 40 training steps, exceeding the highest score attained by random task selection after 120 steps. It also improves downstream performance across model sizes at the same training budget.

items.title_en: DriveOSS: Dataset and Benchmark for 3D Anomaly Segmentation and Open-set Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: DriveOSS：面向自动驾驶中3D异常分割与开放集语义分割的数据集与基准
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in 3D semantic segmentation have significantly improved scene understanding in autonomous driving. However, existing methods are typically developed under a closed-set assumption and evaluated under standard driving conditions, where all categories are known in advance. In real-world driving, autonomous vehicles inevitably encounter previously unseen objects, making closed-set perception insufficient for safe deployment. To address this challenge, we introduce DriveOSS, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first real-world multimodal dataset and benchmark specifically designed for 3D anomaly segmentation and open-set semantic segmentation. It contains 12,661 synchronized and annotated frames captured using six surround-view RGB cameras, a 128-beam LiDAR, and a GPS/IMU unit. The dataset comprises 52 real-world driving scenes collected under clear, nighttime, cloudy, rainy, and snowy conditions and is organized into ID (in-distribution) and OOD (out-of-distribution) subsets. The ID scenes contain only known classes and are used for training, whereas the OOD scenes additionally contain unknown objects annotated as the outlier class and are used for validation and testing. Extensive experiments show that unseen objects remain a major challenge for current 3D perception systems. The dataset, benchmark protocols, and code are available at https://github.com/chrisyan/DriveOSS.

items.title_en: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement
items.title_zh: RESPLE2：面向带全局精化的多传感器里程计的惯性信息递归非均匀样条估计
items.abstract_en: We present RESPLE2, a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion representation. By exploiting the knot-clamping boundary property, we propose a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter, we perform this prediction using a subset of inertial measurements. A subsequent reset step preserves trajectory consistency as the knots extend. The update step further incorporates heterogeneous sensor measurements at their native timestamps through continuous-time observation models, supporting flexible combinations of LiDARs, cameras, inertial measurement units, and leg kinematics. We further develop a lightweight global optimization module that directly refines non-uniform B-spline control points by incorporating loop-closure constraints derived from LiDAR-visual cues. We conduct extensive evaluations on public and experimental datasets across handheld, tracked, legged, and hybrid aerial-legged platforms, covering highly dynamic maneuvers with extreme accelerations. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-sensor odometry systems, RESPLE2 achieves competitive or superior estimation accuracy and robustness in the corresponding sensor configurations, particularly under aggressive motion, while maintaining real-time operation. We publicly release our code and experimental datasets at https://github.com/ASIG-X/RESPLE2.

items.title_en: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation
items.title_zh: 以运动学约束为参照的铰接物体操作评估
items.abstract_en: Manipulation policies are evaluated predominantly by binary task success, which cannot tell whether the commanded gesture is the one the object's kinematics admit. We introduce Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), which projects the commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis, separating progress along the joint from off-constraint waste. CRS requires a joint model and a joint-following scripted controller derived from it, but no recorded demonstration or learned judge. On 74 simulated articulated objects, success registers three transfer failures as lower rates but attributes none, while the two CRS channels give each a distinct signature. A door-trained behavior-cloning policy opens drawers in 59 of 110 episodes, and in these passes it commands about $40\times$ the off-axis rotation of a drawer-trained policy's passes ($1.27$ vs.\ $0.032$~rad/s). Relative to a scripted controller scored with the same axis, CRS verdicts are unchanged under joint-axis errors up to $30^\circ$; absolute thresholds tolerate about $8^\circ$.

items.title_en: When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Adaptive Residual Correction for Robot Policies
items.title_zh: 何时、何处与何物需纠正：面向机器人策略的人类引导自适应残差校正
items.abstract_en: Imitation policies that reliably execute most of a manipulation trajectory can still fail in localized regions requiring last-mile precision. Updating the full policy or exploring residual actions everywhere treats this local failure as a global learning problem. We introduce Adaptive Residual Correction (ARC), a lightweight post-training module that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn a residual correction on top of a frozen policy while using sparse human corrections to structure autonomous exploration. Rather than treating human corrections as imitation targets, ARC uses pre-intervention states to determine 'when' residual control should become active and correction geometry to determine 'where' in residual action space autonomous refinement should explore; task reward determines 'what' residual is ultimately executed. Across three precision-manipulation tasks on a real robot, ARC improves average task success from 33.3% to 75.0%. The human corrections define task-dependent 2-3 dimensional subspaces of the seven-joint residual space that retain 96.0-97.7% of squared correction magnitude. Together, these results show that sparse human corrections can localize and constrain autonomous post-training without requiring the observed correction itself to serve as the final action target.

items.title_en: Rendering-Free Event Frame Simulation for Fast Reinforcement Learning of Autonomous Robot Navigation
items.title_zh: 面向自主机器人导航快速强化学习的免渲染事件帧仿真
items.abstract_en: Event cameras offer low latency, high dynamic range, and milliwatt-level power consumption, making them ideal for agile robots such as tiny drones navigating through cluttered environments. However, existing simulators generally render photorealistic images before converting them into events, making large-scale reinforcement learning prohibitively slow. We propose an analytic event simulator that exploits what event cameras fundamentally measure - moving contrast edges - to synthesize event streams directly from scene geometry and ego-motion without visual rendering. Our simulator generates a 64x64 event observation in 17 microseconds on a single GPU - over 400x faster than a state-of-the-art rendering pipeline - enabling end-to-end reinforcement learning for goal-directed obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes - three orders of magnitude faster than training on rendered events. Policies transfer zero-shot to physically based event simulations (ray-traced Isaac Sim). Our policy reaches 83% success in cluttered courses unseen during training (mid-difficulty, traversability probability approx. 0.57), at 2.4 m/s average goal velocity, and retains 70% in a simulated texture-dense indoor hall. Furthermore, we quantized the policy to a 1.2 MB int8 network running fully onboard a 56-gram Crazyflie equipped with a Prophesee GenX320 event camera and an OpenMV N6 microcontroller board. Without any fine-tuning, external processing, or positioning, the policy achieves an average success rate of 82% (5/5, 5/6, 4/6 flights) across three real-world obstacle courses of increasing difficulty. Code: https://github.com/tudelft/rendering-free-event-nav
authors: Guido C. H. E. de Croon

items.title_en: Predict the Swing, Match the Speed: Robotic Pipe Stabbing With Learned Stereo Vision and Residual Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 预测摆动，匹配速度：基于学习型立体视觉与残差强化学习的机器人管道插接
items.abstract_en: A joint of pipe run into the hole swings from the elevator over the well and strikes a fixed stabbing guide at whatever speed the swing has. StabBot, a robotic stabbing system, predicts the swing and meets the pipe at its own speed. A pendulum Kalman filter tuned from the pipe tally tracks the joint in stereo images. A six-axis arm with an open V-shaped roller head closes in at matched velocity, confirms the last millimetres by touch, aims the pin over the box when the elevator hangs off centre, and follows the block down with lateral compliance. A ResNet-18 keypoint network locates the pipe, pin nose and box mouth in 3-D, and a residual reinforcement-learning policy refines the capture. On 200 paired random jobs with nine sizes from 2-3/8-in. tubing to 20-in. casing, StabBot seated every joint with the pipe touching only rollers, against 74% for a conventional fixed guide. Median contact speed fell from 18.4 to 2.3 cm/s and median peak head-pipe force from 11.3 to 1.4 kN, and the force was lower in all 200 jobs (Wilcoxon $p < 10^{-30}$). The network locates the pipe with 0.4-mm median error in 2.3 ms per stereo pair. With the network in the loop, success stayed at 100% under 20 mm of added noise, 300-ms delay, 85% frame loss, 20-mm calibration offset, 20-cm elevator offset and 40-cm swings. All results come from a 1:4 Froude-scaled MuJoCo model and are reported at full scale.
items.comment: 18 pages, 9 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to Geoenergy Science and Engineering

items.title_en: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use
items.title_zh: 哪只手迟了？面向双臂工具使用中机器人故障恢复的诊断
items.abstract_en: Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration. Bimanual tool use adds failures of other kinds: a tool that slips out of its socket while still held, two correct gestures made at different times, and attempts that fail for two reasons at once. On a simulated bimanual tool-use task whose failure causes are read from the recorded trace, we measure what each sensing channel lets a diagnoser tell. The tool's slip is read on the tool hand; which hand was late is read on both arms, while a sensor on one hand reads its own hand's delay and at most part of the other's; and whether a late attempt was also pushed too weakly is not identifiable from passive sensing when the tool hand is late. Within two attempts, a repair policy that escalates when the cause is not identifiable repairs as many failures as one told the true cause. A VLM's internal state carries the late hand almost perfectly, along a direction no closer to the one its answer reads than a random one; whether the answer reports it depends on the wording of the question.

items.title_en: Leveraging Distributed Sensing and Hyperdimensional Computing for Non-Line-of-Sight Passive Object Sensing
items.title_zh: 利用分布式感知与超维计算进行非视距无源目标感知
items.abstract_en: In smart factory environments, passive entities such as humans and movable obstacles may interfere with autonomous robot operations, posing significant safety risks. Detecting potential conflicts between robots and entities outside their field-of-view (FoV) is therefore of paramount importance. However, conventional passive object detection systems rely on sensors such as LiDAR, radar, or cameras, which operate under direct line-of-sight (LoS) and are limited by obstacles and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables environmental perception via the communication infrastructure thanks to cooperation among distributed wireless devices. In this paper, we propose a framework for passive entity sensing beyond the robot's FoV that relies solely on distributed channel measurements from the communication infrastructure to perform risk-aware classification. These measurements are embedded into high-dimensional representations using hyperdimensional computing (HDC), enabling robust and scalable learning without explicit channel reconstruction. Numerical simulations based on a commercial ray tracer and ROS-based validation in realistic smart factory scenarios demonstrate improved safety and enhanced path planning with up to 89% accuracy under severe occlusions, while maintaining low computational complexity.
items.comment: To appear in the Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC), 2026

items.title_en: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
items.title_zh: Ego-CEVR：从人类自我中心视频中学习跨具身视觉表征
items.abstract_en: As egocentric video becomes increasingly available for embodied learning, an important research question is how to turn this low-cost, scalable source of data into robot manipulation capabilities. Egocentric videos naturally provide rich context for high-level task understanding, while real-robot demonstrations with wrist observations and action annotations provide supervision for fine-grained action alignment. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns object relations, task state, and temporal progress through future prediction on egocentric video. The Interaction module interprets wrist observations in global context and learns local alignment and contact cues through robot action supervision. Separate residual paths expose both representations to the action policy, preserving direct access to task context alongside fine-grained execution information. Ego-CEVR supports independent pretraining of its global video module on large-scale human egocentric videos and videos from diverse robot embodiments, without requiring robot action labels or paired wrist observations.

items.title_en: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
items.title_zh: 基于强化学习的自主固定翼拦截
items.abstract_en: Medium altitude, long endurance unmanned aerial systems such as Shahed-type strike drones are an unanswered threat in modern conflicts. Conventional air defense systems are too expensive to provide a feasible large-scale solution. Quadcopter interceptors are a cheap, battle-proven alternative, but their extremely limited flight time restricts them to low altitude targets at short range, whereas fixed-wing platforms have the endurance to reach higher altitude targets from longer distances. However, such interceptors are still operated manually. Recent developments in learning-based controllers show potential for automation. In this work, a fixed-wing interceptor is presented that is controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands. The policy was trained in a custom Python environment using reinforcement learning and proximal policy optimization. The policy was then deployed on a fixed-wing platform and tested in real interception scenarios. As a baseline, two classical guidance controllers were also developed and tested in simulation. The policy is able to intercept targets both in simulation and in real flight. In simulation, the policy outperforms the classical controllers under most conditions. The interceptor was ultimately successfully validated in real flight by intercepting maneuvering fixed-wing targets. This novel system shows the potential of artificial intelligence for autonomous control of fixed-wing interceptor drones.

items.title_en: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making
items.title_zh: 面向神经决策的可解释元策略
items.abstract_en: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks. While (neuro-)symbolic approaches improve transparency by incorporating symbolic reasoning, applying them directly to low-level actions results in overly complex, unreadable policies. We introduce NEXUS, a hierarchical RL framework that resolves this tension by combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By shifting transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, NEXUS drastically reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and the design of reward functions and meta-policies by interaction with LLMs. We demonstrate that NEXUS agents learn disentangled skills, are interpretable regarding high-level goals, are better aligned to goals described in the game manual, less prone to reward hacking and more robust to game simplifications than deep RL. Finally, we isolate and evaluate the impact of different meta-policy architectures (neural, symbolic, neuro-symbolic) on environmental return and aligned task performance.

items.title_en: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
items.title_zh: 用于降低代谢能量的协同自适应髋关节外骨骼控制的多智能体强化学习（MARL-Exo）
items.abstract_en: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how mechanical-power shaping affects the learned assistance. Methods: We developed MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which a full-body human model (304 muscle actuators; randomized anatomy, gait, and speed) and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy are trained concurrently in two stages. The exoskeleton observes only delayed hip kinematics and its past commands; its reward includes muscle metabolic power from a physiologically based energetics model, alone (Metabolic) or with mechanical-power shaping (Metabolic + Power). The Metabolic policy was deployed and tested without retraining in eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, using indirect calorimetry. Results: In simulation, the Metabolic policy reduced modeled muscle metabolic power by 13.8% relative to no-device walking, versus 8.8% for Metabolic + Power. On hardware, MARL-Exo reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 $\pm$ 6.6% relative to Passive in all eight participants. Relative to No-Exo, the mean reduction was 7.4 $\pm$ 10.0%; six participants more than offset the 13.1% device-wearing penalty, walking up to 24.2% below their No-Exo cost. Conclusion: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit. Significance: Unlike per-user human-in-the-loop optimization, this approach yields a single population-level controller and allows assistance objectives to be screened in simulation before human testing.

items.title_en: VERA-Hand: A Verified Multidimensional Benchmark for 2D Hand Pose Estimation in Third-Person Dynamic Gesture Videos
items.title_zh: VERA-Hand：面向第三人称动态手势视频中二维手部姿态估计的经校验多维基准
items.abstract_en: Hand landmarks serve as input for gesture recognition, sign language understanding, and touchless human-computer interaction. Yet hand pose estimators are typically evaluated with frame-wise localization metrics such as PCK or MPJPE, which are computed over matched predictions and overlook missed or spurious hands, handedness errors, and temporal instability. To address these limitations, we present VERA-Hand, a benchmark that evaluates estimators using manually verified, frame-level 2D annotations for 10,690 hands across four complementary dimensions (detection, localization, identification, and temporal stability), as well as a joint Pose-F1 metric that requires both correct detection and accurate localization. Evaluating six estimators spanning hand-specific, whole-body, reconstruction-based, and foundation-model paradigms, we find that no estimator dominates: rankings reorder sharply across dimensions. VERA-Hand also exposes failures that localization-only and downstream evaluations may not reveal, including cross-hand overlap in over 85% of frames for a recent foundation model. A post-hoc cleanup case study demonstrates how the benchmark can validate corrective interventions, while stratified analyses show that robustness varies across motion-blur classes and hand regions. We release the verified annotations, protocol, and code at https://gibranbenitez.github.io/VERA_Hand/

items.title_en: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
items.title_zh: 利用迭代事后重标记学习质量可控的机器人策略
items.abstract_en: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion. In real-world deployment, however, desired execution behaviors are also defined by quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness, which need to be dynamically controlled according to task requirements. To address this, we introduce Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations. To extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations, we further propose an iterative hindsight relabeling loop: QCP collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, relabels the accumulated trajectories in hindsight according to their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval demonstrate that QCP consistently improves both task execution quality and success rates across iterations, producing successful rollouts that exceed the quality of the initial demonstrations. Finally, we validate QCP on real-world manipulation tasks, where controlling speed increases throughput in conveyor operations and controlling transport stability improves success when carrying wine glasses, demonstrating that quality-controllable policies yield practical gains in physical deployment.

rm.usage: 通过事后重标记实现可控制执行速度与运动平滑度的策略，可用于仿真中训练哨兵导航或工程机械臂的路径策略，让同一策略在推理时按比赛节奏调节激进或保守程度。

items.title_en: VLA-Stem: A Lightweight Safety Mechanism for Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: VLA-Stem：一种通过强化学习为视觉-语言-动作模型提供的轻量级安全机制
items.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate high-level reasoning with low-level action execution for end-to-end robotic control. However, most VLA models target static manipulation in unconstrained environments, overlooking spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. Fine-tuning VLAs on obstacle-avoidance data is a straightforward solution, but collecting such data is costly, especially for dynamic scenarios, and may degrade their original task capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose VLA-Stem, a lightweight, reinforcement-learning-based safety mechanism for VLA systems. Without fine-tuning the underlying VLA policy, VLA-Stem converts its action chunks into motion references and uses trajectory-level guidance to preserve their spatial intent while allowing flexible motion and timing adjustments. Conditioned on these references, robot proprioception, and local obstacle information, the Stem policy adaptively modifies execution at inference time, preserving the original task intent while enabling responsive adaptation to spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. For robust and sample-efficient training, we combine teacher-student distillation with curriculum learning. We evaluate VLA-Stem on reference following, static spatial constraints, and dynamic obstacle avoidance. Across six constrained simulation settings, VLA-Stem achieves 52.8% average collision-free task success versus 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline, while preserving base-policy performance in obstacle-free settings; real-world experiments further show consistent collision reductions under static and dynamic obstacles. These results demonstrate that VLA-Stem couples high-level VLA task intent with rapid, reflex-like responses to immediate physical risks, providing a brainstem-inspired mechanism for robust robot execution.

rm.usage: 用强化学习给视觉语言动作模型加轻量安全约束、处理动态障碍，其「安全层」思路可参考用于哨兵导航与工程机械臂在有人、有障碍场地中的避障兜底，但 VLA 大模型本身不适合机器人端算力。

items.title_en: Tokens of Motion: Primitive Motion Learning for Human-Humanoid Skill Transfer
items.title_zh: 运动令牌：面向人-人形机器人技能迁移的基元运动学习
items.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a promising paradigm for scalable robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on success-only behavioral cloning leaves them brittle; lacking corrective training signals, minor execution errors rapidly compound into unrecoverable, out-of-distribution failures. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL), an end-to-end framework that leverages failure trajectories as adaptive negative guidance for diffusion- and flow-based VLA policies. AFIL uses a pretrained VLA to generate failure rollouts online, avoiding the need for handcrafted failure-mode design or human-in-the-loop recovery. It then jointly trains Dual Action Generators (DAGs) for successful and failed behaviors while sharing a common vision-language backbone, enabling efficient failure-aware policy learning with limited parameter overhead. During sampling, the failure generator adaptively steers action generation away from failure-prone regions and toward more reliable success modes, with guidance strength determined by the per-diffusion-step distance between success and failure distributions. Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain robotic manipulation tasks, covering both short- and long-horizon settings, show that AFIL consistently improves task success rates and robustness over existing VLA baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness, efficiency, and generality.

rm.usage: 把失败轨迹当作负向引导来训练扩散或流式策略，可用于仿真中自瞄、导航等任务：把脱靶、撞墙等失败样本回收进训练，缓解成功样本稀疏的问题。
rm.task: 算法仿真与验证

items.title_en: ScIntBench: Physical Interaction Plausibility in 3D Scene Generation
items.title_zh: ScIntBench：三维场景生成中的物理交互合理性
items.abstract_en: Existing evaluations of text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation largely emphasize semantic fidelity and physical validity at rest, leaving interaction-time physical reliability insufficiently assessed. To address this gap, we introduce ScIntBench, a unified benchmark centered on interaction readiness: it executes prescribed manipulation actions (e.g., pushing, opening, and surface probing) in physics simulation and measures task success, capability and progress, post-interaction integrity, and dynamic plausibility. Multi-view semantic and static physical evaluations complement these metrics and help explain interaction outcomes. We systematically evaluate 12 state-of-the-art scene generation systems across 10 room types. Our results reveal that strong semantic and static physical performance does not necessarily translate into interaction readiness: a system with near-perfect static plausibility completes only 11.54% of interactions, 7 of the 12 systems produce scenes that cannot support any interaction, and even the best system succeeds in only 36.92% of prescribed tasks. These findings highlight two fundamental challenges in generating interaction-ready scenes: providing the necessary physical interaction capabilities and ensuring reliable physical behavior under active manipulation.

rm.usage: 三维场景生成中的物理交互合理性评测基准，对构建仿真场地时评估物体可推、可开等交互合理性有间接参考，但与比赛机制关系很弱。

items.title_en: Hierarchical Sparse Graph for Multi-dimensional Assignment in Event-based Tracking
items.title_zh: 用于基于事件跟踪中多维分配的分层稀疏图
items.abstract_en: Existing event-based tracking methods typically operate in an online manner, associating tracklets across adjacent batches. However, this limited temporal window often leads to failures in challenging scenarios, such as long-term occlusions or missed detections, where broader temporal context should be incorporated for high-precision tracking. To achieve robust and accurate tracking, this paper concentrates on the event-based multi-dimensional assignment that associates tracklets across multiple batches simultaneously. Unlike image-based detectors, event-based detectors can generate multiple correct yet spatially distinct tracklets for a single object per batch. This violates the one-to-one rule in classic data association, making event-based association an underdetermined many-to-many matching problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to tackle this NP-hard problem. To address its underdetermined nature, we formulate the assignment problem via fuzzy logic, where pairwise tracklet correlations are quantified through multiple long-range kinematic metrics. This fuzzy design eliminates the need for hard tracking thresholds and enables multiple heterogeneous metrics to be integrated into a unified correlation. By treating tracklets as nodes and their fuzzy correlations as edges, we construct a Hierarchical Sparse Graph (HSG). Building upon the HSG, we pose assignment as a graph partition task, and employ a heuristic solution that measures vertex affinity for partitioning adaptively. The entire pipeline is training-free. Comprehensive experiments on two challenging event datasets, eTram and Ev-UAV, show that our method outperforms existing event-based and most image-based association models. Particularly, it achieves over 2$\times$ the performance of OC-SORT across all metrics in the many-to-many association scenario.

rm.usage: 其跨批次轨迹片段关联（多维分配）思路可直接迁移到雷达多目标跟踪的数据关联环节，缓解长时间遮挡、漏检导致的 ID 切换；自瞄的短时目标跟踪也可借鉴其时间窗扩展策略。但事件相机与 RM 相机不匹配，需改造成普通帧检测的轨迹关联。

items.title_en: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning
items.title_zh: 关系何时值得信任？多关系图学习中的操纵成本、暴露与信任陷阱
items.abstract_en: Multi-relational graph detectors learn from clean data how much to trust each relation, but an adversary pays a different price to manipulate each relation and each action; taking such costs as given, we ask when using a relation is worse than ignoring it. Our first main result proves that degree gating strictly beats every selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and that this window is sharp; on real graphs, validated gating gains exactly on the relations that meet these conditions and nowhere else. Our second shows that a per-node exposure bound, which extends to message passing, tells a platform which relation to harden: exposure per unit cost, computed without any attack, picks the relation whose hardening raises the exact trap threshold most in 15 of 16 cases, against at most 7 for informativeness, cheapness, or an analysis with equal edit costs. Supporting tools give exact worst cases for linear relational models, certified brackets for R-GCN and tree ensembles, and a finite-sample guarantee for adversarial validation, under which clean-trained graph detectors fall below their graph-free counterparts in 58 of 90 settings on six graphs. A selection protocol built on these results is never significantly worse than ignoring the graph; with at most four relations it mostly abstains, as validation alone would, and its cost-aware proposals help when relations are many, so far shown on synthetic graphs. Without cost information, the safe choice is to abstain.

rm.usage: 讨论多关系图检测器对关系信任的操纵成本与门控机制，属于图学习对抗鲁棒性理论，和自瞄、导航、决策等环节都无直接对应，最多在赛前数据增强/鲁棒性讨论中作为概念参考，实用价值很低。

items.title_en: Remember Where You Walk: Learning Spatial Memory for End-to-End Legged Robot Exploration
items.title_zh: 记住你走过的地方：面向端到端腿足机器人探索的空间记忆学习
items.abstract_en: Humanoids and other legged robots operating in complex environments must remember information that leaves their field of view and only becomes relevant much later. Reinforcement learning policies address this using memory networks such as LSTMs that are trained end-to-end with the policy to memorize such task-relevant aspects. Yet, such architectures often fail to preserve sufficient information over long horizons. In this work, we propose a network architecture based on Hadamard memory that specifically targets robot navigation. Our Local Spatial Matrix Memory (LSMM) enables RL agents to store generic task-relevant information at specific, position-based memory cells, enabling flexible and spatially grounded memorization. We evaluate LSMM on the task of autonomous maze exploration, where it matches the maze coverage of strong recurrent and finite-history baselines while being the only architecture that remembers the maze layout, reducing the reconstruction error threefold.

rm.usage: LSMM 的局部空间记忆结构可借鉴到哨兵机器人：用显式空间记忆记住已探索区域、敌方出现位置与增益点状态，弥补 LSTM 长时程遗忘，提升无通信条件下的自主巡逻与决策；需把腿足探索任务改造为赛场栅格/关键点记忆。
